title: Trace the interface, then interpret the experiment
introduction: Choose a route and a compartment to inspect its place in the tissue. Then compare a prediction with the evidence. These are anatomical maps and fixed research scenarios, not a numerical permeability simulation.

routes.label: Blood → brain tissue
routes.title: Parenchymal capillary route

steps.label: Blood in a CNS capillary
steps.detail: Start inside the vascular lumen. A blood concentration does not by itself establish the concentration in neural tissue.

steps.label: Capillary endothelium
steps.detail: This is the principal sealing cell layer. Intercellular junctions restrict paracellular passage, while low nonspecific transcytosis limits a different, transcellular route.

steps.label: Basement-membrane and support-cell environment
steps.detail: Pericytes and astrocytic endfeet participate in regulation and organisation outside the endothelium. They are not a substitute name for the endothelial junctions.

steps.label: Brain interstitial fluid
steps.detail: This is outside the vascular lumen and surrounds neural tissue. Entry into a particular cell still involves another membrane and its transport processes.

routes.limit: A simplified path through a typical parenchymal capillary, not every CNS vascular region. Card spacing does not represent thickness, time or permeability.

references.title: Daneman et al. — pericytes during barrier development
Ben-Zvi et al. — MFSD2A and endothelial transcytosis

routes.label: Blood → ventricular CSF
routes.title: Choroid-plexus route

steps.label: Blood in a choroid capillary
steps.detail: Start inside a vessel in the core of a choroid frond. Its lumen is distinct from the ventricular space outside the frond.

steps.label: Fenestrated capillary endothelium
steps.detail: Exchange can carry material from blood into the stromal compartment. This is not a direct opening into ventricular CSF. Individual fenestrations are not resolved in the supplied H&E image.

steps.label: Stromal extracellular space
steps.detail: Material here remains on the basal side of the epithelial covering. Reaching stroma does not establish entry into CSF.

steps.label: Choroid epithelial layer
steps.detail: Adjacent epithelial cells form the principal blood–CSF junctional seal. The basal side faces stroma; the apical side faces CSF. Transcellular transport and paracellular restriction are distinct.

steps.label: Ventricular CSF
steps.detail: This is outside the frond, against the apical epithelial surface. A concentration sampled here is not automatically the concentration in brain interstitial fluid or inside a neuron.

routes.limit: A simplified blood-to-ventricle route. Arrows order anatomical interfaces; they do not mean unrestricted flow, a fixed flux or absence of transport in the opposite direction.

references.title: Xu et al. — early postnatal choroid NKCC1 and CSF clearance
Praetorius and Nielsen — human choroid transporter localisation

cases.title: A junctional perturbation
cases.observation: After claudin-5 loss in a late-embryonic mouse model, smaller tested tracers enter brain tissue while larger comparators remain restricted. Vessel morphology is broadly preserved.
cases.question: Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: The observed change is selective for the tested tracer conditions.
options.explanation: Supported. Retain tracer chemistry, exposure and detection conditions. The result does not establish a universal cutoff for every molecule.

options.text: The larger tracers must cross at the same rate if circulation is intact.
options.explanation: Preserved circulation and morphology do not imply identical permeability for different tracers.

options.text: An adult human drug with the same mass will show the same entry.
options.explanation: That extrapolates across compound properties, developmental stage and species without direct evidence.

references.title: Nitta et al. — claudin-5 deletion and tracer selectivity

cases.title: A route through the cell
cases.observation: In an Mfsd2a-deficient mouse preparation, a tracer is seen beyond endothelium and in more endothelial vesicles, while junctional contacts still arrest it.
cases.question: Which mechanism fits these observations most directly?

options.text: A choroid epithelial junction has opened.
options.explanation: This observation concerns parenchymal capillary endothelium; it does not measure the choroid epithelial boundary.

options.text: Increased vesicular transport through endothelial cells.
options.explanation: Supported. Tracer localisation along a transcellular route helps distinguish it from passage between cells.
The reported junctional arrest and vesicular localisation do not support that exclusive route.

references.title: Ben-Zvi et al. — MFSD2A and endothelial transcytosis

cases.title: Two water-related measurements
cases.observation: AQP1 loss reduces osmotic shrinkage of isolated mouse choroid plexus, but does not reduce the in-vivo CSF secretion estimate under the conditions tested.
cases.question: What should be retained when explaining the result?

options.text: Osmotic shrinkage and net secretion are interchangeable measures.
options.explanation: The preparation, imposed driving force and measured output differ.

options.text: A single water-channel image predicts the whole-organ secretion rate.
options.explanation: Molecular location alone does not measure net fluid production.

options.text: Membrane osmotic permeability and system-level secretion are different readouts.
options.explanation: Supported. Report both results with their conditions; do not claim that all water exchange has stopped.

references.title: Jensen et al. — choroid AQP1, NKCC1 and distinct transport readouts

cases.title: Identity versus growth
cases.observation: Reducing Shh signalling in a developing mouse hindbrain choroid system reduces growth and folding while differentiated epithelial markers remain detectable.
cases.question: Which follow-up separates retained identity from normal function?

options.text: Measure organisation and a relevant transport outcome independently of marker detection.
options.explanation: Supported. Retained marker identity does not establish normal architecture or physiological output.

options.text: Treat marker detection as a quantitative secretion measurement.
options.explanation: The readouts differ. A marker can remain while tissue amount or function changes.

options.text: Assign every responding cell to the ligand-producing lineage.
options.explanation: Signal source, pathway response and ancestry require different evidence.

references.title: Huang et al. — Shh-responsive hindbrain epithelial progenitors
